stem.en: Kabir crosses a double hybrid, TtRr, with a pure short-wrinkled plant, ttrr. What ratio does the square predict?

text.en: One to one to one to one. The double hybrid gives TR, Tr, tR or tr equally; the other parent gives only tr. Four kinds of child, equal.
Nine to three to three to one.

feedback.en: That ratio needs two hybrids. Here one parent gives only recessive factors, and every child shows whatever the hybrid gave.
Dominant shows when present. The hybrid gives a t half the time and an r half the time.

text.en: Three to one for each trait, so three to one overall.

feedback.en: A hybrid crossed with a pure recessive gives one to one per trait, from VIII.2 L02. Two independent one-to-ones give four equal kinds.

explanation.en: Write what each parent can give. Multiply. The test cross with a double recessive reveals the hybrid's four combinations directly, which is why Mendel used it.
